name: heterotypic-regions
title: Heterotypic tissue regions: a vertex epithelium on a munk mesenchyme, coupled at an interface
question: Can one tissue be composed of two compartments simulated by DIFFERENT mechanics -- a vertex epithelium sitting on a center-based munk mesenchyme -- coupled at their interface?

study_card.goal: Model a tissue cross-section as two tissue types, each simulated by the mechanics that fits it.
study_card.mechanism: The epithelium (a sheet) is a vertex backend; the mesenchyme (loose cells) is a center-based munk backend. They share a domain and are coupled at their interface: the epithelium's basal edge is a reflective floor the mesenchyme presses up against but cannot cross.
study_card.why_before_next: A different KIND of multi-tissue composition from the consensus: not three paradigms on one cell set, but two tissues of different types meeting at a boundary -- the way real organs layer epithelium on stroma.
study_card.expected_result: A vertex epithelium and a munk mesenchyme coexist in one tissue, coupled at an interface the mesenchyme cannot cross -- two tissue types, two physics, one composite.
study_card.main_expert_question: Should the coupling be bidirectional -- the mesenchyme pushing the epithelium up (buckling it) -- rather than only the epithelium confining the mesenchyme?

behavior_tests.name: both-tissues-coexist
behavior_tests.description: Both compartments persist together (>=16 cells: the vertex epithelium and the munk mesenchyme coexist in one domain).

behavior_tests.name: interface-holds
behavior_tests.description: The interface functions as a boundary: at most a few mesenchyme cells breach it per step before being reflected, so the mesenchyme does not flood through the epithelium.

conclusion_verdicts.if_primary_tests_pass: A vertex epithelium and a munk mesenchyme coexist in one tissue, coupled at an interface the mesenchyme cannot cross -- two tissue types, two physics, one composite.
conclusion_verdicts.if_primary_tests_fail: A collapsing compartment or an interface the mesenchyme floods through would mean the two tissues do not couple.
